name: Secular liberalism
summary: Secular liberalism is liberalism that insists on a state separate from religion: religious ideas and scripture carry no special authority in lawmaking, while freedom of thought, conscience and religion is protected for everyone except where it infringes others' rights. It favors liberal democracy, equality before the law and an open society, and stands opposed to theocracy and religious authoritarianism. It prescribes no economic programme; adherents range from market liberals to welfare-state liberals.
scope: The Anglo-European liberal tradition read through Locke, Mill's On Liberty, Rawls's political liberalism as summarized in the Stanford Encyclopedia, the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and Wikipedia's description of secular liberalism (including the UK Liberal Democrats and outspoken secularists such as Dawkins, Hitchens and Harris). It excludes state atheism, the militant laicism of some regimes, and the Arab-world 'secular liberal' trend discussed only in passing. Because the label is liberalism plus secularism, answers on economics, foreign policy, technology and ecology are mostly low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: John Locke
keyFigures.role: Founder of liberal limited-government and consent theory, cited in SEP as the model of liberalism's basic task.

keyFigures.name: John Stuart Mill
keyFigures.role: Author of On Liberty, source of the harm principle and the case for free discussion.

keyFigures.name: John Rawls
keyFigures.role: Developer of political liberalism, neutrality among comprehensive doctrines and public reason.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The label carries no health policy; most secular liberals in Europe and the Lib Dems back publicly funded care, and SEP notes new-liberal welfare-state strands, so this is an inference.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: SEP shows liberals split between market-first and welfare-oriented strands, and secular liberalism as defined takes no wage position.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Classical liberals hold this and new liberals doubt market stability (SEP), so adherents split.

public-ownership.rationale: Liberals generally prefer private ownership with regulation; SEP ties liberty to private property, though some accept public utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Rawlsian liberals accept redistribution while classical liberals resist it; the secular label itself is silent.

unions-good.rationale: Freedom of association is a liberal value but the label takes no stance on unions; strands differ.

property-fundamental.rationale: Classical liberals treat property as near-fundamental, while Mill and Rawls treat it as an open question (SEP), so split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Strand-dependent: new liberals favor regulation, classical liberals oppose it; no stated position for secular liberalism.

cut-welfare.rationale: Most liberals accept some welfare (Bentham, Green, Rawls in SEP); only the libertarian end would cut it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not a liberal programme; liberal tradition favors private ownership, with worker cooperatives tolerated as a voluntary choice.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Liberals stress privacy and limits on state power; UDHR Art. 12 protects against arbitrary interference with privacy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Mill's harm principle says the individual is sovereign over his own body and mind; secular liberals commonly extend that to adult drug use, though this is applied, not stated, in the excerpt read.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Split: Mill's case for free discussion pushes against restriction, while UDHR Article 7 protects against incitement to discrimination.

strong-leader.rationale: Liberalism is about limited government and the rule of law binding rulers (SEP on Magna Carta); a leader bypassing checks is contrary to it.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberals hold that government is justified and necessary for protecting equal liberty; anarchism is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: No liberal doctrine on guns; liberals divide between rights-based and harm-based arguments.

empower-police-military.rationale: Liberal suspicion of concentrated state power suggests reluctance, but this is inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Mill's principle that adults may act freely absent harm to others supports decriminalization; secular liberals typically follow it, though liberals are not unanimous.

rehabilitation.rationale: Humane, rights-based penal views are common among liberals, but the sources do not discuss prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Mill attacks custom as a guide and secular liberals do not treat traditional family forms as foundational or privileged.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Secular liberalism is associated with social equality and equal rights; UDHR Art. 16 gives adults equal marriage rights without limit by religion, and secular liberals back it strongly.

abortion-legal.rationale: Religious arguments carry no special authority in lawmaking (Wikipedia), and bodily autonomy fits Mill; adherents mostly support legal abortion though some dissent.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wikipedia lists as a core position that religious ideas carry no special authority in public debate and the state is secular.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Equal rights regardless of race (UDHR Art. 2) and Rawlsian fair equality of opportunity support remedies; the extent is disputed among liberals.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not a liberal doctrine; adherents differ, with many accepting mixed nature and nurture.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Mill distrusts custom and tradition as such, but liberals do not oppose cultural heritage; mildly negative inference.

gradual-change.rationale: Liberals support reform through law, but the label does not endorse deference to established institutions; splits.

reduce-immigration.rationale: UDHR Art. 14 and liberal universalism lean toward openness; the secular label itself does not address immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Kant's liberal peace confederation and UDHR show an internationalist strain, but the sources do not set a secular-liberal position.

free-trade.rationale: Classical liberals favor it and most liberals follow, though the secular label is silent on trade.

nation-first.rationale: Liberal universalism and Kantian confederation tilt against nation-first, inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: SEP shows Mill skeptical of intervention and Rawls allowing it against outlaw states; liberals divide.

open-borders.rationale: UDHR guarantees leaving and asylum but not entry, and liberals divide on open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: No secular-liberal position; liberals generally favor growth with environmental regulation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Secular liberals generally accept scientific consensus and public action, though the label states no environmental policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Enlightenment optimism is liberal, but secular liberals are not committed to technological solutionism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No stated position and liberals split.

revolution-justified.rationale: UDHR preamble prefers rule of law so people need not rebel; liberals accept resistance to tyranny only as a last resort.

experts-over-public.rationale: Liberals value democratic consent but also reason and evidence; the label is silent so a mild lean against expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Liberals hold that markets or private property best fit liberty (SEP); even new liberals did not endorse central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not a liberal programme per se; some liberal-socialist strands accept it, others do not.

land-value-tax.rationale: Georgism is a fringe liberal strand, not mainstream secular liberalism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Rawlsian liberals favor it and classical liberals oppose; no secular-liberal position.

basic-income.rationale: Liberals of both new and classical strands have proposed it, but there is no common position.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Liberals mostly oppose protection; inferred from free-trade liberalism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial planning conflicts with liberal market preferences, inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rawls's property-owning democracy is one strand, but not a secular-liberal commitment.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Contrary to the liberal commitment to private property and exchange.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Only libertarian liberals favor this; mainstream liberals accept central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages conflict with liberal individualism and freedom of association.

one-party-rule.rationale: UDHR Art. 21 requires authority resting on genuine periodic elections with equal suffrage, which single-party rule excludes; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Constitutional monarchies exist in liberal states, but secular liberals defend rule by consent and not monarchy as such.

democracy-best.rationale: Wikipedia says adherents usually favor liberal democracy and the open society; the phrase "even when voters choose badly" tempers it since liberals also want constitutional limits.

direct-votes.rationale: Liberals typically prefer representative democracy with constitutional limits, inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Government by the will of the people through equal elections (UDHR Art. 21) excludes councils replacing parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Liberals disagree between consent-based and territorial-integrity views.

natural-rulers.rationale: UDHR Art. 1 and 2 give everyone equal dignity and rights without distinction, rejecting natural hierarchy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Split: liberals reject political violence as a method but accept resistance to tyranny.

war-builds-character.rationale: The liberal tradition of Kant and Mill aims at peace; glorifying war is alien to it.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wikipedia lists formal constitutional separation of church and state as the defining position of secular liberalism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Wikipedia says scriptural arguments carry no special authority in social and political debate and the ideology stands opposed to theocracy.

private-courts-defense.rationale: SEP says even libertarian liberals grant the state a justice and protection role; mainstream liberals reject privatizing courts.

military-superiority.rationale: Liberal states maintain defense, but nothing in the sources asks for superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 and equal rights regardless of ethnicity or religion contradict an ethnically defined nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Liberals do not see history as class conflict; the claim is Marxist.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rawls and others stress equal liberty and fair opportunity, with inequalities allowed if they benefit the worst off, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No stated position; liberals disagree about group rights versus individual rights.

colonial-reparations.rationale: No stated position and liberals split on collective historical liability.

civilizational-union.rationale: Secular liberals reject religion-defined political unions; separation of religion and state is central.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Classical liberals defend self-interest, but Kantian and Millian strands emphasize duty and development.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Liberalism puts individual rights first (Rawls's equal basic liberty), not communal duties.

limit-population.rationale: Compulsory limits would conflict with liberty and UDHR privacy and family rights, inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Liberals from Mill onward view modernity as progress.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Liberal faith in progress and open inquiry leans toward welcoming change, though disrupting institutions is not endorsed; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Mill's principle that the individual is sovereign over body and mind suggests permissiveness, inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Consent-based, accountable government implies human democratic control, inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Privacy against arbitrary interference (UDHR Art. 12) supports encryption, inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Mill criticizes custom as obstacle to progress; liberals favor open-ended improvement.

direct-action.rationale: Change through elections and law is preferred (UDHR Art. 21), though peaceful protest is accepted.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts liberal progress and modern rights.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Contradicts liberal market and specialization views.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Liberals mostly reject need-based distribution as the general principle, though Rawls allows a social minimum.

production-for-use.rationale: Not a liberal principle; liberals accept profit-motivated markets.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim that liberals reject.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by one class over others contradicts equality before the law (UDHR Art. 7) and government by genuine elections (Art. 21).

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Liberals tend to hold the opposite: Kant's liberal peace says commerce and republics favor peace.

taxation-theft.rationale: Only libertarian liberals say it; SEP holds even they accept necessary taxation for protecting liberty.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill states that the only justification for compelling someone against his will is preventing harm to others, and Wikipedia says freedoms are limited only where they infringe on others' rights.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberalism grounds rights in persons (Rawls's equal basic liberty), though the group right to religious freedom is accepted.

conscription.rationale: Liberal reluctance to compel citizens, but some liberals accept it in emergencies.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Kukathas stresses exit rights, but mainstream liberals treat voting and exit as complementary and do not rank exit above democracy.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens are rights-holders, not customers; this is a libertarian fringe idea.

positive-liberty.rationale: SEP shows Green and Tawney endorse positive liberty and Berlin and Hayek reject it, so adherents split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a secular-liberal view; it is a critic's claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: UDHR Art. 1 and 2 equal dignity; liberals reject racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Liberals favor individual suffrage through elections (UDHR Art. 21), not corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: SEP says the basic task of Locke-style limited government is protecting equal liberty, which a state directing every area of life contradicts.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not a liberal theme; it is a nationalist and fascist one.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Liberals follow Kant's peaceful confederation of states.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by consent and law replaced personal loyalty authority.

bound-labor.rationale: Compelled bound labor contradicts the equal freedom in UDHR Art. 1 and the liberal commitment to liberty; the source does not discuss serfdom itself.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Secular liberals appeal to reason and open debate; Wikipedia notes religious ideas have no special authority, implying a shared standard of reason, so they reject strong relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Kantian and rights-based liberals affirm universal moral claims; Rawls's political liberalism is cautious, hence not strongest.

single-common-good.rationale: Rawlsian neutrality among comprehensive doctrines and reasonable pluralism (SEP) denies a single common good worked out by reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not a secular-liberal position; secular liberals divide.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: UDHR Art. 15 gives a right to nationality, but liberals do not generally support ethnic return rights.

revive-national-language.rationale: Mill's pluralism tolerates language revival as a cultural choice but secular liberalism has no language policy.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not a core liberal programme; strands divide.

school-vouchers.rationale: Classical liberals favor and others oppose; label silent.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Classical liberals favor balanced budgets; Keynesian new liberals accepted stimulus (SEP).

economic-freedom.rationale: Hayek says so while Mill treats it as open (SEP); strand dependent.

rule-by-example.rationale: Liberalism relies on law binding rulers (SEP on Magna Carta), not rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.rationale: UDHR Art. 21 will of the people, but secular liberals do not frame it as national right.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Wikipedia says religious ideas have no special authority and secular ethics matter, but liberals like Rawls allow faith as personal motivation, so reason is guide for public justification, not "only".

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Universal rights language (UDHR Art. 2, 22) leans against exclusion, inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Liberals prefer voluntary cooperation to class framing but the sources set no industrial-relations model.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Hostile to culture destruction; liberals value free cultural development.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 and 16 give men and women equal rights and Wikipedia associates the ideology with social equality.

ban-interest.rationale: A rule of religious law, which secular liberals say has no authority in lawmaking.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 bars distinctions by race and Art. 7 requires equality before the law, which segregation law contradicts directly; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist claim; liberals see the state as protecting equal liberty.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No stated position; mild lean from environmental liberalism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Mill's defense of diversity of ways of living argues against enforced cultural assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim; liberals reject it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Liberal parties often favor it (Lib Dems), but liberalism itself has no position.

national-mission.rationale: Kantian liberalism opposes imposing governments on others; Rawls tolerates decent societies (SEP).

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Associated with social equality and equal rights for women; adherents commonly accept structural disadvantage, though it is not stated outright.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: UDHR Art. 16 free marriage and founding a family and Art. 12 privacy of family conflict with state discouragement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Rule of law binding rulers (SEP) and accountability fit liberalism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Only the libertarian end of liberalism holds this (SEP); mainstream secular liberals accept more.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: UDHR Art. 16 says adults may marry without limitation by race, nationality or religion; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: UDHR Art. 1 says all are born equal in dignity and rights and Art. 7 equality before the law; Rawls's equal basic liberty rests on equal standing.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no liberal stance.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources give no liberal view on settler states, and liberals split on historical-justice claims.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equality before the law (UDHR Art. 7) and separation of religion from state favor common civil law regardless of religion, though liberals accept some accommodation.

restrict-conversion.rationale: UDHR Art. 18 includes the freedom to change one's religion, and Wikipedia lists freedom of religion and conscience; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious prohibition; secular liberals say religious ideas lack authority in law and Mill allows restrictions only to prevent harm.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Wikipedia says secular liberals support teaching religion as history and culture and oppose presenting it as fact in schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: SEP says Locke-style liberals hold that only consent-based limited government is justified and citizens are sovereign in a right to say no; UDHR Art. 21 says authority rests on the will of the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is rejected by free-trade liberals, inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority conflicts with UDHR Art. 2 equal rights without distinction and Art. 15 protection against arbitrary loss of nationality.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian non-aggression axiom; mainstream secular liberals accept state coercion for justified purposes.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mill sees competition of ideas and ways of living as beneficial, but struggle between peoples is not liberal.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Split: liberals divide between militant democracy and freedom of association.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Pettit's republican view is listed in SEP as one strand of liberty, alongside negative and positive freedom, so adherents split.

separated-powers.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism restricting rulers (SEP on Magna Carta, dispersal of power) supports checks, though SEP does not discuss it directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rawls's difference principle supports it while classical liberals reject it.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Property-owning liberals favor it while welfare liberals worry about housing stock, so no common position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Freedom of association and employers' rights pull in opposite directions in liberal thought.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian argument is not liberal doctrine.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: UDHR preamble says rights should be protected by the rule of law, and liberals resist emergency suspension.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mill defends complete liberty of discussion, which government control of media denies; UDHR Art. 19 protects free expression.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army conflicts with civilian state accountable to the electorate.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Universal rights language favors easier naturalization, inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Kantian confederation supports it, but the sources do not set a position.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism favors parliament's control of the executive.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Secular liberals leave church organization to churches; they would not impose a governance model, so slight rejection.

clerical-rule.rationale: Wikipedia says secular liberalism stands opposed to theocracy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist doctrine alien to liberalism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Mill's harm principle rules out compelling people for their own moral good, and he defends complete liberty of discussion.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism favors limits on executive power.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Liberal internationalism and Kant's confederation of states favor cooperation over isolation; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Mill's attack on custom and liberal values of pluralism do not endorse romanticizing rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Self-determination by the will of the people (UDHR Art. 21) would decide it, so the label itself takes no side.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: A populist claim opposed by liberal valuing of education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Split: liberals divide between universal standards and pluralist respect, with Rawls tolerating decent non-liberal societies.

death-penalty.rationale: Liberal human-rights thinking leans against capital punishment, but the sources read do not address it and liberals are not unanimous.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Secular liberalism supports teaching without religious dogma and is associated with social equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Wikipedia says secular liberals oppose presenting religion as fact in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Mill's harm principle opposes restriction of adult consumption, though some liberals support limited restrictions.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic citizenship conflicts with universalism, inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Liberal tolerance of minority culture supports it, but SEP does not address.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Split: the SEP records disputes over whether free exercise includes exemptions, with Macedo sceptical and others supportive.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill argues that custom tyrannizes and that social pressure rivals law, and his case for eccentricity is in later chapters than the part read, so medium.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Liberals disagree between contract sanctity and global-justice arguments (SEP cosmopolitans), with no secular-liberal position.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Liberal view treats political independence and constitutional rights as sufficient foundations, inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Government by the will of the people (UDHR Art. 21) supports elected constituent processes, inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberalism ranks civil and political liberty first; UDHR Arts. 19 and 21 protect them.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Cosmopolitans like Pogge and Nussbaum say yes; state-centered Rawls and Miller say no (SEP).

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: No stated position; liberals split between deterrence and disarmament.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: UDHR Art. 21 favors elected government but liberals accept both parliamentary and direct election of presidents.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Mainstream liberal economics favors it, inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Classical liberals reject it and social liberals accept; strand split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate internal to the Marxist left on which liberalism takes no side.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Liberals dispute whether to regulate before scientific proof; the sources are silent.

collective-defense.rationale: Liberal internationalists often back alliances, but the sources give no secular-liberal stance.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Separation of church and state typically implies civil authority over clergy, though liberals oppose hostile curbs; moderate agreement.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional monarchies and ceremonial presidents both exist in liberal democracies.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Liberal consent theory is uneasy with it, inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements are compatible with liberalism but are not a defining position.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Wikipedia says religious ideas carry no special authority in politics, and rule rests on consent not divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Classical liberals sometimes favor flat tax while Rawlsians favor progressive tax, per SEP's strands.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: SEP says the rule of law binds the king, Magna Carta tradition.

space-expansion.rationale: Nothing in liberalism or secularism addresses space policy.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism favors checks, but the classical mixed regime of few and many is not its doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Cult of the leader contradicts limited government and equality.

equal-parenting.rationale: UDHR Art. 16 gives equal rights in marriage and its dissolution, but a legal presumption about custody is a policy choice liberals dispute.

land-redistribution.rationale: Expropriation conflicts with property rights, though compensated reform is accepted by some.

refugee-return.rationale: UDHR Art. 14 and 15 protect asylum and nationality for individuals, but extending return to descendants divides liberals.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Conflicts with liberal universalism and sovereign states.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: UDHR Art. 18 protects changing one's belief, which punishing apostasy directly denies; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mill's harm principle denies state compulsion of private conduct.

common-currency.rationale: No liberal doctrine on currency unions; liberals support both national and shared currencies.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Liberals accept minority cultural institutions but also favor equal individual citizenship.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Equal rights in the country of residence (UDHR Art. 2, 7) matches liberal universalism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Liberals credit ideas as well as economics.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is standard liberal view, inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Classical liberals oppose bailouts and Keynesian liberals defend them, per SEP's divide over market stability.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism and equal basic liberty (Rawls, SEP) constrain majorities; Mill warns of majority tyranny.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Free-trade liberals and social liberals disagree, and the sources set no position.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: UDHR Art. 1 and 7 equality before the law; liberalism historically opposed aristocratic privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Secular liberalism favors teaching history without sacred or nationalist framing, inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: SEP notes Mill's endorsement of despotism over barbarians as an embarrassment; modern secular liberals reject it.

patriotic-education.rationale: No stated position; liberal neutrality in schools suggests mild opposition.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Liberals divide between color-blind equality before the law (UDHR Art. 7) and remedial preferences.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Liberal opposition to empire suggests reluctance, though soft-power influence is not ruled out; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Secular liberalism is associated with social equality and UDHR Art. 2 and 7; classical liberals might allow it, so only mildly negative.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Wikipedia lists constitutional protection of freedoms of thought and conscience and SEP traces constitutional limits on rulers, so entrenched rights fit, though neither source names entrenchment.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: No stated position; the sources do not address colonial borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: UDHR Art. 21 says authority rests on the will of the people through periodic elections; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

minority-veto.rationale: Liberals protect individual rights but not individual vetoes over collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Locke-style liberalism (SEP) holds that limited government rests on consent and breach forfeits it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Liberals disagree between parliamentary and constitutional supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Bentham's utilitarian line; the secular label does not state it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Bentham's concern with suffering supports humane-use rules while accepting use; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Liberals ground obligation in rights and justice, not aristocratic duty.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is a Marxist account liberals typically do not adopt.

native-born-offices.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 and 21 equal access to public service without distinction.

party-own-road.rationale: A dispute inside the communist movement with no bearing on liberalism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Liberals disagree on aid versus trade-led development, and the sources set no position.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist claims clash with consent-based politics and peaceful settlement; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Contradicts equal rights and equal political participation.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Liberal tradition from Hayek onward condemns both together.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Contradicted by historiography; no liberal support.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Mill's free discussion allows debate over monuments, but liberals split between preservation and removal.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Equal treatment (UDHR Art. 2) would support attention to any disadvantaged group, but the label gives no ranking of causes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection supports equal services for victims, but liberals disagree about the empirical premise.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: UDHR universalism holds democracy and rights apply everywhere; though Rawls tolerates decent societies (SEP).

paid-care-work.rationale: Liberal strands differ on whether the state should pay for domestic labor.

filial-duty.rationale: Liberals treat family duties as private and voluntary, with no stated secular-liberal position.

office-by-exam.rationale: Merit-based civil service suits liberalism but the doctrine does not rank it against election or patronage.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: UDHR Art. 16 equal rights in marriage and its dissolution; Mill's liberty favors free choice, and secular liberals reject religious divorce restrictions.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Liberal representation allows judgment, not delegation (inferred).

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Classical liberals favor private accounts and social liberals favor pay-as-you-go pensions.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism since Magna Carta binds rulers to consent for taxes (SEP consent tradition).

single-official-language.rationale: Mill defends diversity; liberals tolerate multilingualism, though many accept a common language.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Equality before the law (UDHR Art. 7) is intent-based for some liberals and outcome-aware for others.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Mill's harm principle suggests individuals choose their own lives; no stated position.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Kant's liberal peace norms of non-interference lean against covert arming, though liberal interventionists disagree.

corporate-influence.rationale: Market liberals deny it while reformist liberals share the concern; the label is silent.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: UDHR Art. 19 protects freedom of expression across borders, so restrictions on funding sit uneasily; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Liberal neutrality in family choices, inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: UDHR Art. 17 protects owning property and liberals dislike discriminatory limits; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: SEP describes Kant's liberal peace of constitutional states.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Consent theory implies obligation to just governments; liberals generally do not deny a duty.

non-intervention.rationale: SEP shows Mill's skepticism but Rawls permits intervention against outlaw states.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is an internal labor-movement question that liberalism does not address.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 and 7 equal treatment and secular liberal equality conflict with blaming a minority; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: UDHR Art. 16 recognizes marriage; liberals reformed rather than abolished it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: UDHR Art. 19 right to seek information; liberal accountability, inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Liberals prefer constitutional parties and open association, though they accept informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Liberals divide between human-rights universalism (UDHR) and constitutional sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Contradicts separation of religion and state and equal rights regardless of religion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not a liberal-secular question; liberals take varied stances.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Liberals hold private property in general, so the distinction is moot and no answer is stated.

defeat-communism.rationale: Liberals disagree between containment and coexistence.

religion-illusion.rationale: Split: outspoken secularists such as Dawkins, Hitchens and Harris agree, but the political doctrine does not require the claim.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 and 16 support equal rights, but liberals disagree that economic transformation is needed.

socialized-care.rationale: Liberals treat housework and childcare as choices of families, with public support optional; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Mill's liberty of speech and diversity oppose purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Liberal rule of law favors honoring treaties, but the sources do not discuss indigenous treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary communities are tolerated (Nozick's utopia in SEP's context), but reorganizing society is not a liberal aim.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement to alter a region's balance conflicts with equal rights without distinction (UDHR Art. 2); inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Liberals typically identify with market economy.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Secular liberalism denies religious claims special authority.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Secular liberals ground public argument in reason and evidence, so they reject denial; liberals may still oppose criminalizing it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Mill's harm principle permits state coercion only to prevent harm to others, and UDHR Art. 12 protects private life.

suppress-opposition.rationale: UDHR Art. 19 and 21 guarantee expression and genuine elections, and Mill defends complete liberty of discussion.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Wikipedia says religion has no special authority and freedoms of thought and conscience are limited only to protect others' rights; Mill opposes persecution.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious obligation not endorsed by secular liberals.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Wikipedia says secular liberalism stands opposed to theocracy and religious authoritarianism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Liberals prefer representative democracy but accept participation.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Associated with social equality and rights; secular liberals mostly support it, though not stated.

assisted-dying.rationale: Individual sovereignty over body and mind (Mill) and secular rejection of religious objections lead most to support.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Liberal centrists say yes; others no.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist concept; liberals do not generally frame wage work as alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Wikipedia lists freedom of religion and conscience for all as core, so secular liberals reject treating one faith as incompatible with liberal society.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: SEP says liberal authority rests on consent of the governed, not on divine sources; Wikipedia says religious ideas carry no special authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Split: secular liberals divide between French laicite and British accommodation.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: No stated position; rule of law and equal protection, inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Centrist liberals broadly accept a market economy with protections; strand dependent.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Liberals accept defense; SEP says even minimal states defend.

rich-first.rationale: Liberal development thinking allows uneven growth but no source states a secular-liberal view.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: No stated position; liberals favored both alignment with democracies and neutrality at times.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is an anarchist programme foreign to liberal markets.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Liberals split between fiscal discipline and sovereign choice; no stated position.

property-franchise.rationale: UDHR Art. 21 states equal suffrage for everyone, which a property qualification denies; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Hegelian concept not part of liberal analysis.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist critique; Mill's liberty-of-discussion defends press freedom as real freedom.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: SEP traces rule of law, equality before law and due process from Magna Carta through Locke; rulers bound by standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 bars distinction by race in rights and Art. 21 gives equal suffrage, which a racial franchise denies; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

online-participation.rationale: Liberals favor participation but the sources do not address online deliberation.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: UDHR Art. 16 says marriage may not be limited by religion, which the restriction would do; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Discrimination against a religious minority conflicts with UDHR Art. 2 and 7 equality.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Liberal democracies experiment with assemblies, but the label has no position.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not addressed: secular liberals treat religion as private and take no view on theology, though many favour reform.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Hayek vs new liberals; strand dependent.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: UDHR equal rights, and secular liberalism associated with social equality.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Wikipedia says secular liberalism protects freedom of religion and conscience, so a state promoting atheism is contrary to it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Liberal rule of law needs enforcement.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational and majoritarian designs are both defended by liberals.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Classical liberals favor, but mainstream accepts state aid.

term-limits.rationale: Liberals disagree about term limits, which limit abuse but also voter choice.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a recent proposal outside the classical liberal representative model.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Neither liberalism nor secularism sets public-policy priorities on extinction risk, so adherents have no common view.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Split: secular liberals defend the autonomy of religious bodies while favouring equality.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: UDHR Art. 16 states equal rights for spouses as to marriage, during it and at its dissolution; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: UDHR Art. 21 applies to citizens, and liberals disagree about extending local votes to residents.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: No stated position; liberals divide on nuclear policy.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: No stated position; liberals divide on alliances and basing.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Contrary to liberal acceptance of returns on property.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Sacralizing the nation conflicts with secularity.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Wikipedia says religious ideas have no special authority in politics.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by liberal or secular doctrine.

culture-before-state.rationale: A nationalist sequencing question outside liberal doctrine.

god-not-male.rationale: Not a political question for secular liberals, who leave theology to believers.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Secular liberals leave theology to believers, so no stance on judging scripture this way.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 and 7 equal treatment conflicts with allocating economic life by group.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Boundary drawing for a people is not a liberal-secular question.

independent-unions.rationale: Liberal freedom of association favors unions free of state control; inferred, not discussed in the sources read.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist definitional dispute on which liberalism takes no side.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Liberal strands differ on public versus private water and hospitals.

second-chamber.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism accepts both bicameral and unicameral legislatures.

municipal-property.rationale: Collective local ownership of the means of production departs from liberal private property.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Libertarian municipalism is a left-anarchist programme, not liberal; Kant's confederation is between states only.

family-wage.rationale: UDHR Art. 2 and 16 imply equal treatment of men and women in work, so a male breadwinner wage is not liberal; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Liberals differ between deregulation and consumer protection.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Research funding priorities are not addressed in the sources, and liberals differ on public versus private science funding.

person-over-state.rationale: SEP gives Kantian contractualism: respecting persons means not subordinating them to others' conceptions of the good, and Rawls's equal basic liberty protects each person.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Wikipedia says religious ideas carry no special authority and ethics may be non-religious, so politics should not serve a spiritual nature.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Liberals disagree about entrenching federal powers versus legislative supremacy.

gm-crops.rationale: No stated position, and liberals diverge on the science-versus-precaution issue.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is not addressed by liberal doctrine.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Individual equal rights, not racial blocs.

racial-pride.rationale: Liberals accept ancestry pride as a personal sentiment but reject racial hierarchy (UDHR Art. 1 and 2).

language-defines-nation.rationale: Liberal citizenship rests on equal rights for residents and consent, not on a shared language.

communal-electorates.rationale: UDHR Art. 21 requires equal suffrage and secular liberalism rejects religion as basis of political representation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A conspiracy belief with no basis in liberal thought.

free-public-college.rationale: Social liberals favor it, classical liberals oppose it; no secular-liberal position.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Liberal economists favor pricing externalities, inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Rawls's just savings principle supports duties to later generations, but the sources do not give the position.

arms-reduction.rationale: Kant's liberal peace favors reducing standing armies, but liberals accept defense needs.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Liberal states claim the monopoly of coercion; SEP on state's role protecting liberty.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Freedom of contract and union rights pull in different directions in liberal thought.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Welfare-liberals favor, market-liberals accept and others oppose; no label position.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Classical liberals support rules and Keynesians resist them (SEP).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Cosmopolitan liberals favor and state-centered liberals oppose, per SEP.

nature-as-capital.rationale: A market-environmentalist idea with no secular-liberal position.

sacred-nation.rationale: Wikipedia places secular liberalism against sacralized political authority; sacred community contradicts secularism.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Liberal strands differ on state cancellation of private contracts.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A dependency-theory concept that liberal analysis does not adopt.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rawls bars appeals to comprehensive doctrines; Kantian grounding supports it, split.

public-service-media.rationale: Standard liberal institutional design in Europe, inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Liberals split between subsidiarity and national enforcement of rights; no stated position.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Mill values diversity of ways of living and Wikipedia ties the ideology to equality, so secular liberals reject the claim.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Government by the will of the people (UDHR Art. 21) implies annexation without consent is illegitimate; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from liberal neutrality between religions and non-religion, which treats no faith as the truth the state should assume.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: liberalism prescribes no economic programme and market-minded liberals oppose guaranteed prices, though welfare liberals might accept them.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that adherents are split between liberal internationalists favouring disarmament and those favouring deterrence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from liberalism's individual, non-class basis of representation; liberals generally work through broad parties rather than class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Bodily integrity and equal dignity of women and girls are core human-rights commitments, and religious or customary justification carries no special authority.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Universal Declaration affirms equal rights without distinction of sex and the right to own property, which secular liberals treat as a standard; the Declaration is not a secular-liberal text, so this follows from the liberal principles it codifies rather than a stated position.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; secular liberalism is indifferent to the naming of languages.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: Mill's harm principle supports liability for harm to others' property, but liberals are split on courts versus regulatory agencies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Lawmaking authority rests on consent and equal citizenship under elected institutions, so hereditary or customary authorities get no official legislative role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the priority liberalism gives to individual liberty, limited only by harm to others per Mill.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from rule-of-law commitments favouring proportionality and judicial discretion over fixed penalties.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; liberals are split between integration expectations and opposition to coercion of immigrants.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The label prescribes no economic programme and liberals split on union rules.

voter-id.rationale: Secular liberals prize equal access to the vote but disagree on identification requirements, so neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: State neutrality between religions and between religion and non-religion is the core of the view.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Liberal democracy as defined here includes rights protections and not only elections, so adherents would not accept a purely procedural test.

premarital-sex.rationale: Mill's harm principle leaves private consensual conduct to the individual, and no religious doctrine binds lawmaking.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The Universal Declaration protects freedom of opinion, expression and information, which a liberal reads as ruling out blanket shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Market and welfare-state liberals disagree on welfare design, so neutral.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equality before the law and equal participation in government are core liberal commitments, stated in the Universal Declaration.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Prominent outspoken secularists say yes while many liberals stress religion's varied effects; adherents split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from liberal equality principles and the rejection of ascribed status; the scientific view is not stated in these sources.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from liberal equality before the law; liberals split on whether dedicated agencies are the right tool.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Locke's liberal tradition, as summarised in the SEP, grounds property in labour on unowned things; secular liberals are mostly sympathetic, though welfare liberals qualify it.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Liberal internationalism and the UDHR's emphasis on universal rights support holding leaders accountable before international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Secular liberalism holds that scripture has no special authority in lawmaking and treats it as one belief among many.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Liberal equal-dignity principles (UDHR) imply women's equal participation should be guaranteed in any self-rule; inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Liberals value political freedom and rule of law and would not defend a bureaucratic planned state for its economic system; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: The UDHR calls for genuine elections by universal suffrage; liberals generally prefer direct votes, though indirect systems are tolerated.

national-church-status.rationale: Wikipedia and SEP both give separation of church and state and equal treatment of religions as core, which excludes a privileged national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Liberals are split between individual-rights universalism and accommodation of group autonomy; the sources do not settle it.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Consent of the governed and self-determination point to local votes, though liberals vary on specific cases; inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Liberals are split between stability of inherited borders and self-determination; the sources do not settle it.

simple-living.rationale: Mill's liberalism leaves each person to choose their way of life and does not require limited needs; an ideal of austerity is not liberal doctrine.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The UDHR guarantees freedom of movement and residence within a state, which conflicts with restricting settlement by group.

equal-conscription.rationale: Equality before the law (UDHR) implies any draft should treat women and men alike; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from liberalism's individualist and universalist outlook, which does not treat the nation's land as a spiritual duty.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Liberalism and the UDHR require fair trial and the presumption of innocence, so state killing without trial is rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Liberalism prescribes no preference between trade partners; secular liberals disagree on China versus the United States.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from liberalism's civic, rights-based view of states over ethnic kinship ties.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Liberals are split between those who accept private appropriation and egalitarian liberals such as left-libertarians; the label sets no answer.

self-ownership.rationale: Mill holds that over his own body and mind the individual is sovereign, which supports self-ownership, though not all liberals use the term.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Liberalism prescribes no economic programme; adherents range from market liberals to welfare-state liberals.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Liberals split between universal provision and targeted welfare; the sources describe no common view.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Liberal democracy relies on parties, free association and pluralism, which the UDHR protects, so bypassing them is rejected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from liberal equality before the law, which opposes special legal privileges, though not stated for business specifically.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Secular liberalism holds that the state is separate from religion and gives religious authority no special place in lawmaking, which excludes organising politics by denomination.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from liberalism's progressive, individual-choice orientation, which does not treat a return to ancestral values as a goal.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The UDHR gives men and women equal rights as to dissolution of marriage, and liberal equality supports each spouse's right to leave.

national-resource-control.rationale: Liberalism says nothing about resource ownership; adherents range from free-trade liberals to economic nationalists.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Secular liberalism has no economic programme and market liberals and welfare liberals split on process versus pattern; inferred as neutral.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The label prescribes no economic policy and liberal strands disagree on financial regulation; inferred as neutral.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Adherents hold varied views on how far racism still limits people, and the sources do not address it; inferred as neutral.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to rule of law and procedure, which favours changing unjust laws by legitimate means, though liberals accept civil disobedience.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred as neutral: liberal strands split over automation and work, and the sources do not address it.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the liberal tradition of rights guaranteed by universal standards and institutions, such as the Universal Declaration; adherents are not unanimous.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: liberal economics rests on subjective or market accounts of value, though Mill's classical economics partly used labour costs.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Liberal strands split between cosmopolitan and patriotic views, and the sources do not address it; inferred as neutral.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from the liberal emphasis on equal rights and recognition for every group, which makes identity issues part of liberal politics.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The Universal Declaration calls for genuine periodic elections and free expression, and liberalism pairs markets with limited government, so one-party communist rule contradicts it.

missingStatements.text: Laws that coerce citizens should be justified by reasons all citizens can accept, not by religious doctrine alone.
missingStatements.rationale: Public reason is the central secular-liberal rule for lawmaking, with religious reasons permitted only alongside shareable ones in Rawls's later view.

missingStatements.text: The state should be neutral between religions and between religion and non-religion.
missingStatements.rationale: SEP describes liberal democracy as committed to neutrality toward notions of God and the good, and Wikipedia gives equal protection of belief and non-belief.

notes: Wikipedia's article is short and defines the ideology only through church-state separation, liberal democracy and conscience rights, so most non-religious answers are inferences. Economic answers split along classical versus social liberal lines. Strong-secularist (French laicite) and accommodationist (British, American) strands answer religious dress and exemptions differently.
